public_rationale: Both parts hold for late 2024. Mintz's policy report says the December 2024 defense bill held the first and likely only AI provisions passed by the 118th Congress. Even those provisions do not regulate AI generally, and the comprehensive AI legislation senators called for did not pass. So Congress had achieved little. Anti-regulation figures were winning. In September 2024, Newsom vetoed California's SB 1047 after Andreessen Horowitz and others lobbied against it. On December 5, 2024, Trump named David Sacks, a deregulation-minded investor, as AI czar. Analysts read the appointment as signaling a deregulatory stance on AI.
limitations: 'Little' and 'good run' are vague. The scoring relies on a plain reading.
Mintz is a law-firm policy newsletter, not an official record.
The Mintz NDAA note was published a week after the post, but it describes the state of affairs at the post date.

statement.excerpt: Congress achieved little, and anti-regulation AI folks like Andreeseen are having a good run.

our_interpretation: 'Congress achieved little' means the 118th Congress (2023–2024) had passed no substantial AI regulation by around the post date.

'Anti-regulation folks having a good run' means that, in the period before the post, opponents of AI regulation (Andreessen and his firm, and allies) won notable policy fights or gained policy influence.
Target period: January 2023 (start of the 118th Congress) through December 2024 (the post month).
criteria.support_condition: Records showing no substantial federal AI regulation enacted by the 118th Congress, plus documented policy wins or gains in influence for anti-regulation AI figures in 2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Records showing that Congress enacted substantial AI regulation in 2023–2024, or that anti-regulation advocates suffered clear policy defeats in that period.
